'''Katherina Reiche''' ({{IPA|de|katəˌʁiːna ˈʁaɪ̯çə|lang|De-Katherina Reiche.ogg}}; born 16 July 1973) is a German manager and politician of the [[Christian Democratic Union (Germany)|Christian Democratic Union]] (CDU) who has been serving as [[Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy|Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Energy]] in [[Merz cabinet|the cabinet]] of [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Friedrich Merz]] since May 2025.<ref>{{cite web|author=Sarah Frühauf |url=https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/innenpolitik/minister-union-kabinett-merz-100.html |title=Wen Merz ins Kabinett ruft – und warum |work=Tagesschau |lang=de |accessdate=2025-04-28}}</ref>

From 1998 to 2015, she was a [[member of the German Bundestag]], serving from 2005 to 2009 as one of the deputy chairpersons of the [[CDU/CSU|CDU/CSU parliamentary group]]. From 2009 to 2013, she was [[Parliamentary State Secretary]] to the [[Federal Ministry for the Environment, Climate Action, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety|Federal Minister for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety]], and from 2013 to 2015, Parliamentary State Secretary to the [[Federal Ministry for Transport|Federal Minister for Transport and Digital Infrastructure]]. In September 2015, she resigned her seat in the Bundestag.

==Education==
After receiving her [[Abitur]] in 1992, she studied chemistry at the [[University of Potsdam]], [[Clarkson University]] in New York and the [[University of Turku]] in Finland, where she received her diploma in 1997.

==Political career==
===Early beginnings===
[[File:KAS-Reiche, Katherina-Bild-19709-1.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Reiche on a 1998 election poster]]
In 1992, Reiche was one of the founding members of the ''[[Ring Christlich-Demokratischer Studenten]]'' (Association of Christian-Democrat Students, RCDS) in Potsdam and in the same year she joined the [[Junge Union|Young Union]] (JU). Since 1996 she has also been a member of the [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU]]. 

===Member of the German Parliament (1998–2015)===
In 2000 Reiche became a member of the federal executive of the CDU. From 2001 to 2015, she was also part of the party's executive board in the state of [[Brandenburg]].

During the [[2002 German federal election|election campaign in 2002]], Reiche was part of the CDU/CSU's competence team appointed by then-chancellor candidate [[Edmund Stoiber]] as an expert on women, youth, and family policies. This decision was criticized by conservative circles inside the two parties because Reiche was an unmarried mother at that point in time.

From 2005 until 2009, Reiche served as deputy chairwoman of the [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU]]/[[Christian Social Union of Bavaria|CSU]]'s parliamentary group, under the leadership of chairman [[Volker Kauder]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.cducsu.de/Titel__Katherina_Reiche/TabID__23/SubTabID__24/AbgLetter__82/AbgID__35/Abgeordnete.aspx |title=CDU website |access-date=31 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090122050436/http://cducsu.de/Titel__Katherina_Reiche/TabID__23/SubTabID__24/AbgLetter__82/AbgID__35/Abgeordnete.aspx |archive-date=22 January 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In this capacity, she was in charge of overseeing the policy areas Education and Science as well as Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety.

In the negotiations to form a [[coalition government]] following the [[2009 German federal election|2009 federal elections]], Reiche was part of the working group on the environment, agriculture, and consumer protection, led by [[Ilse Aigner]] and [[Michael Kauch]].<ref>[https://www.spiegel.de/politik/deutschland/koalitionsverhandlungen-wen-union-und-fdp-zum-feilschen-schicken-a-653453.html Koalitionsverhandlungen: Wen Union und FDP zum Feilschen schicken] ''[[Spiegel Online]]'', 6 October 2009.</ref>

===Career in government===
In the government of [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]], Reiche first served as Parliamentary State Secretary at the [[Federal Ministry for the Environment, Nature Conservation and Nuclear Safety]] under successive ministers [[Norbert Röttgen]] (2009-2012) and [[Peter Altmaier]] (2012-2013) from 2009 to 2013. Following the [[2013 German federal election|2013 elections]], she was named Parliamentary State Secretary at the [[Federal Ministry of Transport and Digital Infrastructure]], this time under the leadership of minister [[Alexander Dobrindt]].

On the occasion of the sixtieth anniversary of the [[Germany–India relations|diplomatic relations]] between Germany and [[India]], Reiche participated in the first joint cabinet meeting of the two countries' governments in [[Delhi]] in May 2011.<ref>Günther Bannas (30 May 2011), [https://www.faz.net/aktuell/politik/hoffnung-auf-eurofighter-geschaeft-erste-deutsch-indische-regierungskonsultationen-1640384.html Hoffnung auf „Eurofighter“-Geschäft: Erste deutsch-indische Regierungskonsultationen] ''[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]]''.</ref>

==Career in the energy sector==
In 2015, Reiche resigned from her government office and laid down her parliamentary mandate to become Chief Executive Officer of the German Association of Local Utilities (VKU). In this capacity, she was unanimously elected President of the [[European Centre of Enterprises with Public Participation and of Enterprises of General Economic Interest]] (CEEP) in June 2016.<ref>[http://www.ceep.eu/katherina-reiche-elected-ceep-president/ Katherina Reiche Elected CEEP President] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210111043125/https://www.ceep.eu/katherina-reiche-elected-ceep-president/ |date=11 January 2021 }} [[German Cancer Research Center]] (DKFZ), press release of 8 June 2016.</ref>

From 2018 until 2019, Reiche also served on the German government's so-called coal commission, which was tasked to develop a masterplan before the end of the year on how to [[Fossil fuel phase-out|phase-out coal]] and create a new economic perspective for the country's coal-mining regions.<ref>Andreas Franke (6 June 2018), [https://www.platts.com/latest-news/coal/london/germany-launches-commission-tasked-to-develop-26969439 Germany launches commission tasked to develop coal exit masterplan] ''[[S&P Global Platts]]''.</ref>

In late 2019, Reiche moved to a new position at German energy company [[E.ON]],<ref>Christof Schürmann (11 September 2019), [https://www.wiwo.de/unternehmen/energie/energiekonzern-katherina-reiche-wird-chefin-der-neuen-e-on-netzgesellschaft/25003444.html Katherina Reiche wird Chefin der neuen E.On-Netzgesellschaft] ''[[Wirtschaftswoche]]''.</ref> where she led its subsidiary Westenergie from 2020 to 2025.<ref>Jürgen Flauger (29 September 2020), [https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/energie/energiewirtschaft-eons-neue-netzwerkerin-katherina-reiche-geht-mit-westenergie-an-den-start/26227274.html Eons neue Netzwerkerin: Katherina Reiche geht mit Westenergie an den Start] ''[[Handelsblatt]]''.</ref>

Since June 2020, she has been the chairwoman of the National Hydrogen Council of the [[Federal Government of Germany|Federal Government]].

* [[NRW.Bank]], Member of the Advisory Board (since 2022)<ref>[https://www.nrwbank.de/export/.galleries/downloads/Info-und-Service/Finanzberichte/nrwbank-finanzbericht-2022.pdf 2022 Annual Report] [[NRW.Bank]].</ref>

===Non-profit organizations===
* German Council for Sustainable Development (RNE), Member (2016–2022, appointed ad personam by [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]])<ref>[http://www.nachhaltigkeitsrat.de/presseinformationen/pressemitteilungen/detailansicht/artikel/bundeskanzlerin-beruft-rat-fuer-nachhaltige-entwicklung-neu/ Bundeskanzlerin beruft Rat für Nachhaltige Entwicklung neu] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104141453/http://www.nachhaltigkeitsrat.de/presseinformationen/pressemitteilungen/detailansicht/artikel/bundeskanzlerin-beruft-rat-fuer-nachhaltige-entwicklung-neu/ |date=4 November 2016 }} German Council for Sustainable Development (RNE), press release of 26 October 2016</ref><ref>[https://www.nachhaltigkeitsrat.de/aktuelles/bundeskanzler-beruft-neuen-rat-fuer-nachhaltige-entwicklung/ Bundeskanzler beruft neuen Rat für Nachhaltige Entwicklung] German Council for Sustainable Development (RNE), press release of 18 January 2023</ref>
* [[Deutsche Flugsicherung]] (DFS), Member of the Advisory Board
* [[Deutsches Museum]], Member of the Board of Trustees
* [[Konrad Adenauer Foundation]] (KAS), Member<ref>[http://www.kas.de/wf/de/71.4891/ Members] [[Konrad Adenauer Foundation]] (KAS).</ref>
* Association of German Foundations, Member of the Parliamentary Advisory Board (until 2015)

==Political positions==
In 2005, Reiche described the opponents of [[genetic engineering]] as ''"Bioterroristen"'' ("Bioterrorists").<ref>{{Cite web|title=Personen & Konflikte|url=https://www.publik-forum.de/Publik-Forum-15-2005/personen-konflikte-875|access-date=7 October 2020|website=Publik-Forum.de|language=de}}</ref> She also criticized the two then-governing parties [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]] and [[German Green Party|the Greens]] for trying to catch votes with this subject and stirring up the people's fears for the future.{{citation needed|date=January 2014}}

In 2012, Reiche claimed same-sex marriage was a bigger threat to Germany than the [[Eurozone crisis]]. She was heavily criticized by [[LGBT]] groups for the remark.<ref>{{Cite web|last=reporter3|date=28 August 2012|title=Equality group calls for German politician to retract anti-gay remarks|url=https://www.gaystarnews.com/article/equality-group-calls-german-politician-retract-anti-gay-remarks280812/|access-date=1 November 2020|website=Gay Star News|archive-date=28 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220428090142/https://www.gaystarnews.com/article/equality-group-calls-german-politician-retract-anti-gay-remarks280812/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Reiche is in a relationship with [[Karl-Theodor zu Guttenberg]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.stuttgarter-zeitung.de/inhalt.kuenftige-wirtschaftsministerin-und-ex-minister-katherina-reiche-und-karl-theodor-zu-guttenberg-machen-beziehung-oeffentlich.a36f056d-b08f-4d12-a946-f7377dfd0038.html |title=Künftige Wirtschaftsministerin und Ex-Minister: Katherina Reiche und Karl-Theodor zu Guttenberg machen Beziehung öffentlich |publisher=Stuttgarter Zeitung  |date=28 April 2025 |access-date=28 April 2025 |language=de |trans-title=Katherina Reiche and Karl-Theodor zu Guttenberg make their relationship public}}</ref>
